name: Kinshasa
subtitle: Kinshasa, capital of DR Congo: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,664,200 people live in Kinshasa (the 1984 census, the last one held in the country) (counted 1984).
The last census in the DRC was held in 1984, so all population figures for Kinshasa are projection-based.
Léopoldville, originally Stanley Pool station, arose from Henry Morton Stanley's third expedition to the Congo (1879-1884).

parts.text: The last census in the DRC was held in 1984, so all population figures for Kinshasa are projection-based.
Léopoldville, originally Stanley Pool station, arose from Henry Morton Stanley's third expedition to the Congo (1879-1884).
Léopoldville is named after Leopold II, king of the Belgians, who commissioned the expeditions.
The capital of the Congo was at Boma and was transferred to Léopoldville in 1929.
Kinshasa lies on the bank of the Congo River at the exit of Pool Malebo and the start of the cataracts.
Before 1960 Kinshasa was a commercial centre before becoming an administrative capital.
Léopoldville received civil status as a city, with annexed zones and 11 communes, in 1957.
Kinshasa comprises 24 communes, of which Maluku, Nsele, Mont-Ngafula and Ngaliema are the largest.
The DRC is preparing its second general population census, the first since 1984.

parts.text: 2,664,200 in 1984, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Ville de Kinshasa, 1984 scientific census (the last census held in the DRC); all later figures are projections.

items.text: The post of Léopoldville is dated to 1881, regarded as the starting point of the history of the city of Kinshasa.
The capital of the Congo was transferred from Boma to Léopoldville in 1929.
Léopoldville received civil status as a city with 11 communes.
On 30 June 1966 President Mobutu proclaimed Patrice Lumumba a national hero and announced a large monument to him, the origin of the Limete Interchange.
Work on the Limete Interchange was interrupted between 1974 and 1978.
The 1984 census counted 2,664,200 people in the city of Kinshasa.
A partial rehabilitation in 2011 installed the Museum of Contemporary and Multimedia Art and a 6.5 m statue of Lumumba at the foot of the Limete tower.
The Académie des Beaux-Arts, founded in 1943, celebrated its 75th anniversary in 2018.
The Limete Interchange Tower became the logo of the 9th Jeux de la Francophonie, held in Kinshasa from 26 July to 6 August 2023.
